weekly_highlights.title: US Nonfarm Payrolls Unexpectedly Fall by 23K in July, Missing Expectations
weekly_highlights.summary: US Nonfarm Payrolls declined by 23,000 in July, significantly missing the expected 80,000 increase. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%, while annual wage inflation eased to 3.2%. This weaker-than-expected jobs report led to a drop in the probability of a September Fed rate hike to 46%.
weekly_highlights.indonesia_impact: Weaker US jobs data reduces the likelihood of Fed rate hikes, which could lead to a stronger IDR and increased foreign capital inflows into Indonesian bonds and equities (IHSG).

weekly_highlights.title: US Dollar Index (DXY) Falls After Nonfarm Payrolls, Nearing Two-Month Low
weekly_highlights.summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY) fell by 0.5% to 99.4, near a two-month low, following the release of weaker-than-expected US employment data. This decline was driven by reduced expectations for near-term Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. The DXY has been consolidating for nearly two months, with the NFP report acting as a key catalyst.
weekly_highlights.indonesia_impact: A falling DXY, driven by reduced Fed rate hike expectations, typically leads to IDR appreciation and can encourage foreign investment into Indonesian financial markets.

weekly_highlights.title: U.S. GDP Growth Slows to 1.5% in Second Quarter
weekly_highlights.summary: The advance estimate for Q2 2026 US GDP showed a 1.5% annual growth rate, a deceleration from 2.1% in Q1. This slowdown was attributed to a downturn in government spending and reductions in investments and exports.
weekly_highlights.indonesia_impact: Slower US GDP growth could signal reduced global demand, potentially impacting Indonesian exports. However, it might also lead to a more dovish Fed, which could strengthen the IDR and attract capital flows to Indonesia.

weekly_highlights.title: Gold Rallies to Seven-Week High Despite September Fed Hike Odds
weekly_highlights.summary: Spot gold rose 1.1% to $4,285.89 an ounce, marking a 6% weekly gain, its strongest since January. This rally occurred even as markets priced a 55% probability of a September Fed rate hike. Lower energy prices, reducing inflation concerns, helped gold hold above the $4,000 support level.
weekly_highlights.indonesia_impact: A rally in gold prices generally indicates global risk aversion or inflation concerns, which could indirectly affect investor sentiment towards emerging markets like Indonesia. A stronger gold price might also reflect a weaker USD, which is positive for the IDR.

weekly_highlights.title: S&P 500 Hits 53rd All-Time High of 2024, Climbs Over 27% YTD
weekly_highlights.summary: The S&P 500 index reached its 53rd all-time high of 2024, demonstrating strong momentum with a year-to-date gain of over 27%, following a 26.1% gain in 2023. The market has bounced back after a recent dip, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) and strong earnings reports from major tech companies.
weekly_highlights.indonesia_impact: A strong S&P 500 can indicate robust global investor sentiment, potentially leading to increased risk appetite for emerging markets, including Indonesia, and supporting the IHSG. However, it could also divert capital from emerging markets if US returns are perceived as superior.

weekly_highlights.title: Total Nonfarm Payrolls for July 2026 Projected to Rise By 97,500
weekly_highlights.summary: Prior to the official release, the median estimate for total nonfarm payroll employment for July 2026 was a rise of 97,500, based on 12 estimates collected by FactSet. The median estimate for the unemployment rate was 4.2%.
weekly_highlights.indonesia_impact: This pre-release forecast set market expectations. The actual NFP falling significantly short of this projection subsequently impacted Fed policy expectations, which in turn affects the IDR and foreign capital flows to Indonesia.

major_headline.title: US Nonfarm Payrolls Unexpectedly Fall by 23K in July, Missing Expectations
major_headline.summary: US Nonfarm Payrolls declined by 23,000 in July, significantly missing the expected 80,000 increase. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%, while annual wage inflation eased to 3.2%. This weaker-than-expected jobs report led to a drop in the probability of a September Fed rate hike to 46%.

key_insight.summary: The most significant development this week for Indonesian investors was the unexpected decline in US Nonfarm Payrolls by 23,000 in July, coupled with easing wage inflation. This data, significantly weaker than market expectations, has led to a notable reduction in the probability of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in September, now standing at 46%. A more dovish outlook from the Fed typically translates to a weaker US Dollar (DXY), which fell by 0.5% to near a two-month low. For Indonesia, this scenario is largely positive: a weaker USD tends to strengthen the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR), making imports cheaper and potentially easing inflationary pressures. Furthermore, reduced prospects of higher US rates can enhance the attractiveness of Indonesian assets, such as government bonds (SBNs) and equities (IHSG), by encouraging foreign capital inflows seeking higher yields in emerging markets. While slower US GDP growth could temper global demand for Indonesian exports, the overall impact of a less aggressive Fed is expected to support the IDR and Indonesian financial markets.
